[line]

[font=Tahoma][color=#9900ff][size=6]INFO﻿
[/size][/color][/font][font=Trebuchet MS][size=3]This tool makes creating [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/9969?tab=description]fashion sense[/url] packs a bit easier. It's mostly for those who don't like messing around with .json files. With this tool you just need to type things in and it creates the pack for you. 

Additionally, you can open and edit existing packs with this easily. [/size][/font]


[font=Tahoma][color=#9900ff][size=6]FEATURES
[/size][/color][/font][font=Trebuchet MS][size=3]Keep in mind this tool is a [color=#ff7700]work in progress[/color]. More featuers will be added if wanted or needed.
Currently it only has creation for static sprites, as in I haven't added animation support as of yet.

[list]
[*][font=Trebuchet MS][size=3]You simply fill in the information for your pack, add items, choose their type (accessory, hats, sleeves, shirts..), load your sprite, name your item, edit the positions if needed, add any additional tweaking and save your pack. This will give you a finished pack. If you decide later on that you want to add more, simply open the pack and edit any existing items or add more. You can also duplicate existing items.[/size][/font]
[/list]
[list]
[*][font=Trebuchet MS][size=3]There's a sprite preview where you can see your current item sprite.[/size][/font]
[/list]
[list]
[*][font=Trebuchet MS][size=3]I also added some debugging commands you can copy to use for SMAPI in the settings menu, so you can easily test your pack ingame as you go.[/size][/font]
[/list]
[list]
[*][font=Trebuchet MS][size=3]You can also hover over some of the things if you're curious what they do or what they're for. [/size][/font]
[/list][/size][/font][size=3][font=Trebuchet MS]

[/font][/size][font=Tahoma][color=#9900ff][size=6]INSTALLATION
[/size][/color][/font][font=Trebuchet MS][size=3]Simply extract anywhere.
Don't seperate the things in the folder from each other, otherwise the .exe won't work properly or at all.
If you don't like keeping things in folders, simply create a shortcut for the .exe and place it where you want. That's what I usually do ;P

If you get the pop-up from windows telling you it's harmful, click "run anyway". It's a false positive from windows. This happens with a lot of .exe files.

[/size][/font][line]
